newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway supply board looks at gas links to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Norway supply board looks at gas links to Britain.

text.p: Norway's Gas Supply Committee (FU) is studying possible tie-in points and optimal use of fields and pipelines to support new gas exports to buyers in Britain and Ireland, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
The assessment was requested by the Oil and Energy Ministry and has a deadline of October 1, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.

"In a letter to Statoil, the ministry pointed to the recent agreement between the Norwegian and UK authorities over use of Norway's Frigg pipeline to St Fergus in Scotland and to future export prospects," it said.
Britain previously had been a major buyer of Norwegian gas but failure of Norwegian and British authorities to clarify use of the Frigg system hindered new sales contracts in recent years.
Statoil said the Frigg line could be upgraded to carry almost double current capacity of 6.5 billion cubic metres of gas per year.
Partners in Frigg are Statoil with 29 percent, Norsk Hydro with 32.87 percent, Elf Petroleum with 21.42 percent and Total with 16.71 percent.
